findings.highlight: repelled all of Caster’s spells
findings.evidenceJa: キャスターの神言を全て弾き返し
findings.governingReading: repelling every one of Caster’s Divine Words
findings.explanation: Caster’s specific high-speed spellcraft, Divine Words, is generalized to ordinary spells.

findings.highlight: her footwork, and her attack were perfect
findings.evidenceJa: 踏み込む速度、大地に落とした足捌き、横一文字に振り抜いた剣に是非はない
findings.governingReading: There was no fault in the speed of her advance, the placement of her feet on the earth, or the sword she swept straight across
findings.explanation: The three concrete components of Saber’s flawless execution are collapsed into a generic evaluation.

findings.highlight: A perfect strike that was slashed horizontally
findings.evidenceJa: 横一線になぎ払った必殺の一撃
findings.governingReading: the certain-kill blow swept across in a horizontal line
findings.explanation: The blow’s lethal, fight-ending character becomes the vague praise “perfect,” and the English action is malformed.

findings.highlight: being caught between something
findings.evidenceJa: 何かに刀身を挟まれて停止している
findings.governingReading: the blade has been caught and stopped by something
findings.explanation: “Between something” requires two sides or objects and leaves the stopping action grammatically incoherent.

findings.highlight: experts today who actually use it
findings.evidenceJa: それを実現する達人の事も
findings.governingReading: the masters capable of accomplishing it
findings.explanation: mirror moon adds that such experts exist “today,” a temporal claim absent from Saber’s limited knowledge.

findings.highlight: stop an invisible sword with his bare body
findings.evidenceJa: 必殺の一撃、視えない刀身を捉え、かつ素手で押し止めた
findings.governingReading: caught the invisible blade of a lethal strike and held it fast with his bare hands
findings.explanation: The English drops both the blow’s lethal status and Kuzuki’s two-stage feat of catching and forcibly arresting the blade.

findings.highlight: deep as if coming down from the ground
findings.evidenceJa: 地の底から響いてくるような声
findings.governingReading: a voice that seemed to reverberate from the depths of the earth
findings.explanation: A voice rising or resonating from deep underground is made to come downward from the ground.

findings.highlight: As she has a long weapon, she is at a disadvantage at close range
findings.evidenceJa: 長柄の武器を持つ以上
findings.governingReading: With a long-handled weapon, she is disadvantaged against an unarmed opponent at cross range
findings.explanation: The long handle and the written/reading layer defining cross range as close combat disappear; the following one-step-one-sword distance is likewise reduced to generic short range.

findings.highlight: It is an established rule to pursue a retreating enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 当然逃がすまいと追ってくる敵を迎え撃つのが定石である
findings.governingReading: The standard move is to meet and strike the enemy who naturally pursues rather than let her escape
findings.explanation: Saber’s plan to counterattack a pursuing Kuzuki is changed into a maxim instructing pursuit of a retreating enemy.

findings.highlight: The things aimed accurately at her vital points are human fists
findings.evidenceJa: 的確に急所だけを狙ってくるソレ
findings.governingReading: That which precisely targets only her vital points is unmistakably a human fist
findings.explanation: The source identifies the previously mysterious attack as a human fist; the English turns both subject and fist plural and produces a malformed sentence.

findings.highlight: his mountain-like fingers
findings.evidenceJa: 巌じみたあの指
findings.governingReading: those crag-like fingers
findings.explanation: A hard, rocklike tactile image becomes the much looser and physically misleading “mountain-like.”

findings.highlight: heaviness and intensity as if they are made of iron
findings.evidenceJa: 神鉄で作られたかのような強度と重さ
findings.governingReading: with the hardness and weight of something forged from divine iron
findings.explanation: The supernatural material image and physical hardness become ordinary iron and the abstract “intensity.”

findings.highlight: his forearms that move from there
findings.evidenceJa: そこから更に変化する二の腕
findings.governingReading: the upper arm that changes the trajectory still further from there
findings.explanation: mirror moon substitutes the forearm for the upper arm, corrupting the account of how Kuzuki changes the blow’s direction.

findings.highlight: They are sharp and dull
findings.evidenceJa: 鈍重で鋭利
findings.governingReading: ponderous and sharp
findings.explanation: 鈍重 describes heavy, ponderous movement, not a dull edge; the English makes the paired qualities contradict each other.

findings.highlight: they contain poison that will lead to death
findings.evidenceJa: 死に至る毒を帯びた突起物
findings.governingReading: projections bearing a poison that leads ultimately to death
findings.explanation: The source develops a figurative model for blows that create fatal openings; the English states that the attacks literally contain poison.

findings.highlight: they aren’t that heavy
findings.evidenceJa: 威力はそう大きくない
findings.governingReading: their force is not especially great
findings.explanation: Limited striking power becomes low physical weight, obscuring why the otherwise survivable blows remain dangerous.

findings.highlight: His stance is like his arms, steady like a rock
findings.evidenceJa: その構えは、拳と同じく岩のように不動
findings.governingReading: His stance, like his fists, is immovable as rock
findings.explanation: The comparison shifts from Kuzuki’s fists to his arms and weakens absolute immobility to steadiness.

findings.highlight: her bared head
findings.evidenceJa: 剥き出しである彼女の顔
findings.governingReading: her exposed face
findings.explanation: Kuzuki’s target is Saber’s uncovered face within her guard, not her entire head.

findings.highlight: His right hand that has not been used yet
findings.evidenceJa: 今まで一度も使われなかった右腕
findings.governingReading: the right arm he had not used even once until now
findings.explanation: The carefully reserved right arm becomes merely a hand; the same passage also turns a fist launched like a cannonball into a fist launched “like a cannon.”

findings.highlight: smash her head to pieces
findings.evidenceJa: 完膚無きまでに頭を飛ばす
findings.governingReading: send her head flying so completely that nothing remains
findings.explanation: The predicted result is total decapitation or obliterative removal of the head, not smashing the head into pieces.

findings.highlight: Anchor…!
findings.evidenceJa: 突き刺し針………！
findings.governingReading: Piercing Needle—Anchor…!
findings.explanation: Only the ruby pronunciation “Anchor” survives; the written technique-name image of a piercing needle disappears.

findings.highlight: the attack that passed her uses its fingers to dig into her neck
findings.evidenceJa: 躱された瞬間、音をたてて彼女の首に指を食い込ませた
findings.governingReading: the instant the thrust was evaded, its fingers audibly bit into her neck
findings.explanation: The English assigns fingers to an abstract attack in malformed present tense, obscuring the feint-like change from missed punch to neck grab.

findings.highlight: easily squeeze off her neck
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの首を容易く握り潰していく
findings.governingReading: easily proceeds to crush Saber’s neck in his grip
findings.explanation: The unidiomatic “squeeze off” suggests detachment rather than progressive crushing.

findings.highlight: Her neck is scraped off
findings.evidenceJa: 首の肉を削がれながら投げ飛ばされ
findings.governingReading: hurled away as the flesh of her neck is scraped off
findings.explanation: The English says Saber’s neck itself is scraped off, a far more anatomically final injury than flesh being gouged from it.
